messages:
Maria Chen: quick RFC follow-up — proposing we narrow the metering event contract to a tiny canonical envelope + move heavy attribution blobs into a separate attribution table. want feedback on migration plan and consumer impact.
Alex Park: can you list the exact fields you want in the canonical envelope?
Maria Chen: minimal: tenant_id, event_id, event_time, token_count, model_id, schema_version. everything else (prompt_ids, user_metadata, attribution_trace) moves to attribution_table keyed by event_id.
Sachin Rao: so consumers that just charge tokens keep reading same topic with little parsing changes, right?
Maria Chen: yep. read path for billing stays lightweight. attribution consumers join against attribution_table only when needed. reduces the hot path CPU and serde cost.
Lia Gomez: how do we guarantee consistency for audits? if attribution is separate, a crash between writes could leave mismatch.
Maria Chen: good point. plan is: producer writes envelope to kafka topic A, writes attribution row to changefeed topic B in same producer transaction where possible (kafka-ish txn), and we add short-lived reconciliation: a delta-checker job that looks for envelope without attribution after N mins and flags + retries.
Samir Patel: reconciliation window? sounds like another surface area. is eventual consistency ok for auditors?
Maria Chen: auditors expect determinism. we keep a 7-day reconciliation lookback and a UI in Console showing missing-attribution alerts per tenant. when reconciliation finds missing attribution we backfill via a replay producer that fetches payloads from S3 staging.
Alex Park: migration: do we write both old-style full events and new minimal envelopes for a while? dual-write?
Maria Chen: dual-write for 2 weeks, with a compatibility header `legacy_full_event: true|false`. consumers can switch to minimal envelope when they see `schema_version >= 2`. will expose a feature-flagged canary route in Dedicated.
Sachin Rao: storage costs? moving blobs to attribution_table (BigQuery?) will increase storage but lower egress/compute for billing. we should estimate.
Lia Gomez: prefer partitioning attribution_table by tenant + date, TTL for debug data (90 days), and a cheaper columnstore for long tail.
Maria Chen: agree. suggestion: short-term attribution in Bigtable for quick joins, long-term archived to GCS/BQ with partitioned snapshots.
InfraBot: deploy-checklist: ensure producer lib has `write_envelope()` and `write_attribution()` atomic path, feature flag toggle, reconciliation job, console alerting, backfill lambda.
Samir Patel: testing: can we add a harness that injects missing-attribution cases to validate backfill logic? also add SLO for reconciliation lag (target < 10m for 95pct).
Maria Chen: yes — adding harness + a staged canary in region-us-east1. Also will add a metric `metering.attribution_mismatch_count` and an alert > 0 for 1 minute in prod -> paging to eng-platform oncall.
Alex Park: any read-model changes for reporting? need to check dashboards that currently scan full events.
Maria Chen: dashboards will query a materialized view joining envelope+attribution; we'll maintain legacy view for 30 days. migration doc will list queries to update.
Sachin Rao: one more: what about retries and duplicates? event_id must be idempotent key across envelope and attribution writes. producer lib will dedupe on write side.
Lia Gomez: ok. +1 on TTL and partitioning. also we should document privacy: remove PII from attribution and stash redacted blob only.
Maria Chen: noted. I'll update RFC with: canonical envelope fields, attribution schema, transactional write pattern, reconciliation design, canary plan, monitoring and retention. aiming to start migration next sprint.
Alex Park: LGTM. thanks for summarizing. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: happy to help with the reconciliation job.
Maria Chen: thanks all — will post the RFC update link later.
InfraBot: scheduled pipeline rollout window picked: 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC (dry-run in staging tomorrow).
